info.title: RMB Dubai -- Mobile API (v1)
info.description:
Customer mobile app API for RMB Dubai: registration and KYC, projects and sites, concrete orders, payments and wallet, support.

Bearer token on everything except `/auth/*`.

**Changes in 1.1.0** -- no path or verb changed, so existing clients keep working.

- Auth responses carry `kyc`, `accountState`, `access`, `nextStep`. A business awaiting KYC now signs in and is stopped at payment, not at the door. Branch on `access`, not `is_kyc_verified`.
- Orders gain a `Draft` status and `paymentStatus`. An order stays a draft until payment succeeds.
- `services.pump` is now a type plus a metre range, replacing `size: small|medium|big`.
- `siteAccess.narrowAccess` and `roadPermit` become objects with a `required` flag and an uploaded `fileId`. `boomPumpRequired` removed.
- `imageUrl` populated across catalogue, projects, orders, payments.
- `email` is nullable -- sign-up never collected one.
- `AUTH_FAILED` split into `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` / `NOT_AN_APP_ACCOUNT`; `ACCOUNT_NOT_READY` removed; list endpoints return `200` with `isEmpty` instead of `NO_*_FOUND` 404s.

Full notes: API-DOCS.md

code.description: Machine-readable error code -- branch on this, not on `message`.

fields.description: Present only on validation errors -- one message per invalid field.

KycState.description:
KYC progress for this account.

- `not_submitted` -- registered, no documents uploaded.
- `partially_submitted` -- some documents in, some still missing.
- `under_review` -- everything submitted, with our team.
- `approved` -- cleared; the account can submit orders and pay.
- `rejected` -- one or more documents refused; see `access.blockedMessage`.
- `not_required` -- individual accounts, which have no KYC step.

AccountState.description: Single source of truth for what this account may do.

AccountAccess.description: Capability flags. Read these rather than re-deriving rules from `kyc` -- the boundary between what a pending account may and may not do is deliberately not "everything or nothing".

canSubmitOrders.description: False while KYC is outstanding. The draft is built, then held.

blockedMessage.description: Display-ready. Null when nothing is blocked.

PaymentStatus.description:
Payment progress, independent of `status`.

- `unpaid` -- draft, nothing attempted.
- `awaiting_payment` -- intent created (card / bank transfer).
- `processing` -- proof submitted, staff verifying.
- `paid` -- settled; the order has left draft.
- `failed` -- attempt failed; the order is still a draft.

OrderStatus.description: `Draft` is new in 1.1.0. An order stays there until a payment succeeds. Scheduling only ever sees `Pending` and beyond, so an unpaid order cannot reach a plant.

PumpRequest.description: Replaces the 1.0.0 `{required, size}` shape. Sizes are boom reach in metres and must come from `GET /pump-sizes` -- a range no pump falls inside is rejected with `PUMP_UNAVAILABLE` at order creation rather than discovered on pour day.

SiteAccessAttachment.description: Null until a file is uploaded and attached.

SiteAccessRequest.description: Replaces the five flat booleans of 1.0.0. `boomPumpRequired` is removed -- it duplicated `services.pump` and the two could contradict each other.

fileId.description: Required when `required` is true. Image only.
Required when `required` is true. PDF or image.

OrderSummary.description: The order card, identical across list, home and project detail.

WalletShortfall.description: Wallet balance is denominated in token m³, not AED.

403.description:
Sign-in refused, or verification still outstanding.

`VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` is NOT a failure: it carries a fresh `verificationId` so the app can go straight to the OTP screen rather than making the customer register again.

A business awaiting KYC does **not** appear here -- it signs in with 200 and a `kyc` of `not_submitted` or `under_review`. That is the main behavioural change in 1.1.0.

post.description:
Step 1 of 3. Same two-step shape as the KYC upload the app already implements.

1. `POST /site-access/upload-urls` -> `{fileId, uploadUrl}`
2. `PUT` the raw bytes to `uploadUrl`
3. send `fileId` inside `siteAccess` when creating the order

put.description:
Step 2 of 3. The real MIME type is sniffed from the bytes rather than trusted from the header, so a PDF renamed `.jpg` is rejected.

Narrow access accepts JPG/PNG/WEBP. Road permit additionally accepts PDF.
